title: Prefetching Strategies
description: Learn advanced prefetching strategies to make your React Query application feel instant.

data.text: Prefetching is the practice of loading data before the user explicitly requests it. With React Query, you can prefetch data using `prefetchQuery` and `fetchQuery`, turning reactive data fetching into a proactive strategy that eliminates perceived latency.

Users perceive a site as fast when transitions feel instant. Even if your API is blazing fast, the round-trip time between navigation and data availability creates a perceptible delay. Prefetching narrows this gap by loading data in anticipation of user intent.

data.title: The Perception Gap
data.text: A 200ms network delay feels acceptable on load, but noticeable during navigation. Prefetching bridges this gap by loading data while the user is still on the previous page.

data.title: Benefits of Prefetching
items: Makes the app feel telepathic to the user
Leverages idle time between user actions
Works seamlessly with React Query's cache layer

data.text: React Query offers two programmatic methods for fetching data outside of a component. `prefetchQuery` loads data and populates the cache without subscribing to updates, while `fetchQuery` returns a Promise that resolves with the data. Both are useful, but they serve slightly different purposes.

cards.title: prefetchQuery
cards.description: Populates the cache silently without subscribing. Ideal for pre-loading data the user will need soon.
pros: Cache is populated for future use

cards.title: fetchQuery
cards.description: Returns a Promise that resolves with the data. Useful in event handlers or non-React contexts.
cons: Still populates cache as a side effect

data.text: Hover prefetching is one of the most effective patterns for improving perceived performance. When a user hovers over a link or button, you have a strong signal that they intend to navigate. You can use this idle time to fetch data before they click.

data.title: Debounce Hover Prefetching
data.text: Avoid prefetching on every mouseEnter event. Use a short debounce (50-100ms) to ensure the user is actually hovering intentionally, not just passing the cursor across the screen.

data.text: Many modern routers support route prefetching out of the box. By prefetching the entire page or specific queries on route change, you ensure that when the user lands on a new page, the data is already in the cache.

data.caption: Prefetch data flow from hover to navigation
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant L as Link
    participant Q as QueryClient
    participant A as API

    U->>L: Hovers over link
    L->>Q: prefetchQuery(queryKey, queryFn)
    Q->>A: Fetch data
    A-->>Q: Return data
    Q->>Q: Store in cache
    U->>L: Clicks link
    L->>Q: useQuery(queryKey)
    Q-->>L: Return cached data instantly

data.text: Some pages require multiple queries. You can prefetch them all in parallel to reduce total wait time. Use `Promise.all` with multiple `prefetchQuery` calls to ensure the cache is fully populated before the user navigates.

data.title: Avoid Over-Prefetching
data.text: Prefetching every link on a page can saturate the user's network and waste bandwidth. Focus on high-intent elements like primary navigation, product cards, and pagination links.

data.title: Implement Hover Prefetching on a Product List
data.description: You have a product listing page with links to individual product detail pages. Add hover prefetching so that when a user hovers over a product card, the product detail query is prefetched.
steps: Create a ProductCard component that receives a product object
Use useQueryClient to get the QueryClient instance
Add an onMouseEnter handler that calls prefetchQuery with the product query key
Set staleTime to 5 minutes so prefetched data stays fresh
Verify in React Query DevTools that the prefetch populates the cache on hover
data.expectedOutcome: Hovering over a product card triggers a background fetch. Clicking the link navigates instantly with cached data.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: prefetchQuery loads data into cache without subscribing
fetchQuery returns a Promise with the data
Debounce hover events to avoid wasting requests
Balance prefetching against bandwidth and cost
data.takeaway: Prefetching transforms reactive loading into proactive loading, making apps feel instant.
